title: Time Jump: 06:45, Oil on the Kaw

fields.narration: It is 06:45. STARTEX was one hour ago. The Prairie Line has been shut in since 06:04. Mill Ridge Station at milepost 213.1 and Sandhill Valve at milepost 215.6 have both been closed since 06:09. SCADA volume balance run VB-0620 still reads 2,700 to 3,500 barrels of medium sour crude. The planning figure is 3,100 barrels, and it is still unverified. Since about 06:40, crude has been running out of a drainage ditch and into the Kansas River near the Mill Ridge boat ramp. The river is moving at about 2 knots, so the oil is travelling downstream at roughly 2.3 river miles an hour. The public heard about this from County 911, the county partner page and a Facebook video before they heard anything from Ironbark. Prairie 6 News goes live at 07:00, fifteen minutes from now. The Ironbark IMT is being called out at Level 2. Gordon Iwata is Incident Commander and Cole Whitfield leads the Environmental Unit. One more thing: nobody has written anything in the notification log since the NRC call. Each position, tell the room where you stand against the first-hour notification table: who has been called, at what time, who you spoke to, and what you told them.
worldState: Clock: 06:45. Elapsed since STARTEX: 1 hour. Oil has been in the river for about 5 minutes.
Source: line shut in at 06:04. Block valves at MP 213.1 (Mill Ridge Station) and MP 215.6 (Sandhill Valve) have been CLOSED since 06:09. Cause unknown. Nobody in the field has seen the pipe.

Volume: 2,700–3,500 bbl medium sour crude, planning figure 3,100 bbl, UNVERIFIED. Basis: metered imbalance 05:50–06:04 plus calculated drain-down between the block valves (VB-0620). This is not a worst case discharge.

Oil in water: crude is entering the Kansas River from a drainage ditch near the Mill Ridge boat ramp. Flow is about 8,500 cfs, surface velocity about 2.3 mph. A fisherman has reported a brown sheen moving fast downstream. It has a rotten-egg smell, which points to H2S from sour crude.

Downstream, in order: Mill Ridge boat ramp; piping plover nesting sandbars (miles 6–9); Prairie Bend Rural Water District intake (mile 11); Cottonwood Slough mussel bed (mile 22); Sterling Bluff Water Department intake (mile 34).
The Environmental Unit has not run a trajectory yet. No arrival windows have been issued.

Notifications: Ironbark has reported to the NRC (report 1398274). The NRC has called back asking for an updated quantity and a cause. The on-call QI Teresa Holloway has been paged. Prairie Bend County Emergency Management called Ironbark, not the other way round. Its 06:39 partner page went to the Prairie Spill Response Cooperative duty phone and the Sterling Bluff Water Department plant.
The notification log has no entries after the NRC call. The log has not recorded any call to the OSRO, KDHE, KDEM, either water intake operator, the county, EPA Region 7 or the trustees.
IMT: Level 2 call-out under way (national team of 40 with Ironbark corporate staff). Incident Commander Gordon Iwata, Environmental Unit Leader Cole Whitfield, PIO Beth Aranda.

Public: the @KawRiverCatfishKing post ("10,000 barrels," "water is POISONED") has more than 340 shares. Prairie 6 News has asked Ironbark to confirm 10,000 barrels before its 07:00 live shot. Ironbark has not issued any public statement.
fields.facilitatorNote: Go round the table and ask each role to state its notification status against SNIMTA 2. Expected: NRC done; QI reached; OSRO, KDHE 24-hour spill line, KDEM and both intake operators due by about 06:34. That is 30 minutes from the 06:04 shutdown, so those calls are already late or close to it. County EM is due within 45 minutes and EPA Region 7 and the trustees within 60. Probe two points. First, does the page the county sent to the Sterling Bluff plant count as Ironbark notifying the intake? It does not. Second, does the QI confirm Level 2 because more than 1,000 bbl has reached water? Do not hand out arrival times. The Environmental Unit should work them out from the 2.3 mph river speed.
fields.scenarioTitle: Ditch to Intake: Prairie Line River Crossing Release & Water Intakes

instructorNote: This card resets the room at the one-hour mark and makes every role account for its calls against the SNIMTA 2 first-hour table. Watch for three things: whether a single notification log gets started (who, time, person spoken to, what was said), whether the QI confirms Level 2 because more than 1,000 bbl went to water, and whether anyone counts the county's page as Ironbark's own notification to the intakes.
